## KV-Cache Memory: Capacity, Paging, Prefix Reuse, and Eviction {#sec-ch2}

::: {.callout-note title="Scaffold status"}
Scaffold only: drafting has not yet begun. This page records the approved plan for the chapter; it contains no teaching content, questions, answers, figures, worked examples or citations yet.
:::

**Purpose.** Turn the logical KV-cache size into a capacity plan, and explain how serving engines allocate, share, reuse and reclaim cache memory.

**Prerequisites and planned recap.** Workbook 04 Chapter 3 (KV-cache size), Chapter 4 (sliding windows, latent KV) and Chapter 8 (looped depth); Workbook 05 Chapter 5 (kinds of memory measurement); Chapter 1 of this workbook.

**Scope boundaries.** KV-cache quantization is Chapter 5; preemption policy and cross-machine KV transfer are Chapter 3. Rolling-buffer eviction mechanics need a re-verified source before any mechanism claim.

### Learning objectives

Planned outcomes (approved scope). By the end of this chapter you should be able to:

- Estimate maximum concurrency from a memory budget, separating logical estimates from profiled and observed memory.
- Explain reservation waste and internal and external fragmentation.
- Trace block tables, reference counting and copy-on-write.
- Compare full-block hashing with radix-tree prefix reuse, including the conditions under which a cached prefix may be reused.
- Explain the memory mechanics of preemption by swapping or recomputation, and how engine versions differ.
- State how looped depth can affect cache size.
